record.what_it_does: Customer support helpdesk suite: tickets, help center, messaging, AI agents.
record.auth_notes: Requests use OAuth access tokens sent as 'Authorization: Bearer'. A multi-customer integration must use global OAuth tokens. Global OAuth clients must be requested from Zendesk and approved, and developers cannot create them themselves. Local OAuth clients are fine for internal use. API tokens are deprecated; they use Basic auth in the form {email}/token:{api_token}. The security page documents no password Basic auth for API access; it only describes end-user email/password access. Every account has its own subdomain, so a toolkit must collect the user's subdomain.
record.access_notes: A free 14-day trial lets a developer build and test with a local OAuth client or an API token. Sponsored (d3v-) accounts, which don't expire, are only for Marketplace app developers. Distributing to many Zendesk customers needs a global OAuth client. Zendesk issues these only on request through the Marketplace portal, submitted from a d3v- account, and must approve each request. Production use needs the customer's paid Zendesk plan.
record.api_breadth_notes: The Support/Ticketing API covers tickets, users, organizations, custom objects, and ticket workflows. Separate APIs cover Help Center/Guide, Messaging/Sunshine Conversations, Talk, and more. Well over 100 operations. Zendesk's EAP MCP catalog alone lists more than 400 tools.
record.mcp_notes: Zendesk hosts an official MCP server for each account, e.g. https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/mcp. It is offered under 'Zendesk Bridge / external AI agents' and is currently in an early access program (EAP) that customers must join. It authenticates with an OAuth client and is available on Suite Team and higher and Support Team and higher. The MCP Client, for calling external servers from action flows, is a separate product that is GA. Third-party servers also exist, from Pipedream, Swifteq and reminia, among others.
record.blocker_notes: Development on a free trial with a local OAuth client or API token is self-serve. Shipping a public multi-tenant toolkit needs a global OAuth client, which Zendesk must approve after a Marketplace-portal request from a d3v- sponsored account. Each user's subdomain must be collected.

evidence.quote: Zendesk supports using OAuth access tokens to authenticate API requests.
For security reasons, Zendesk doesn't allow developers to create their own global OAuth clients.
If the request is approved, Zendesk converts your local OAuth client to a global OAuth client.
You can try out the Zendesk platform with a free, 14-day trial account.
You can use the Support API with tickets, users, organizations, custom objects, and manage ticket workflows.
integrations that subscribe to certain activity in Zendesk Support, Guide, Gather, and Messaging.
Zendesk Bridge and external AI agents are currently in an early access program (EAP).
